title: Is AI on your power bill?
summary: AI data centers need huge amounts of electricity. A Senate report, a bipartisan bill and the companies disagree about who pays for the grid upgrades.

say: Your electricity bill might be helping pay for AI.
One 100-megawatt data center can use about as much power as 100,000 homes.
But a report from three Democratic senators says it may employ only about 100 permanent workers.
scenes.label: One 100 MW data center

say: When the grid needs new lines and power plants, that cost is often shared by everyone with a meter.
A Harvard energy-law expert put it simply: everyone pays.
scenes.credit: Ari Peskoe, Harvard Electricity Law Initiative, to NPR

say: In Louisiana, estimates say one giant Meta project could add 8 to 13 dollars a month to the average Entergy bill.
scenes.title: ELECTRIC BILL

say: The report says none of the seven companies it looked at agreed to pay for grid upgrades that only exist because of them.
The companies say they pay their direct costs, and bigger upgrades help everyone.

left.says: None of 7 companies agreed to pay for upgrades built only for them

right.says: We pay our direct costs. Bigger upgrades help everyone.

say: Now two Republicans and two Democrats want new data centers of 20 megawatts or more to cover the extra costs they add to the grid.
scenes.head: U.S. SENATE · BILL
scenes.title: Data centers pay their own way
lines: New data centers of 20 MW or more
cover the extra grid costs they add

say: So, should AI data centers pay for their own power lines? Tell us below.
